sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Shared cards, badges, receipts and meters
sections.what: Styles the basic pieces: cards, status badges with a colour for each data state, receipt drawers, stamps, a ten-block meter, and the first part of the call card (ticket) including its options and lock button.
sections.why: Likely reason: these pieces appear on many screens, so they are styled once here.
sections.watch_out: Badge colour depends on the exact data-state text, so a misspelled state gets no colour.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: Timing tower, chips, share card, crew pages
sections.what: Styles leaderboard rows with rank, form dots and change arrows, the persona chip, the share card with its fixed shape, and the base look of crew pages.
sections.why: The share card's fixed 1200 by 630 shape is named in its component comment, so the card is likely meant to be shared as a picture. Other reasons are not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Long names in the share card may overflow, since only the leaderboard rows cut names short with an ellipsis.

sections.name: File setup (part 3)
sections.title: Crew menu, onboarding and navigation bar
sections.what: Styles the crew menu, the onboarding screens with progress bar and sport choices, and the top navigation bar with its skip link and focus outlines.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The skip link sits off-screen until it has focus, so moving it carelessly could hide it from keyboard users.

sections.name: @media (min-width:768px)
sections.title: Wider-screen navigation and legacy dark panels
sections.what: From 768 pixels wide, hides the menu button and shows the navigation links in one row. Also gives older dark panels their dark background and light text.
sections.why: Likely reason: links collapse into a menu on phones and show in a row on larger screens.
sections.watch_out: On small screens the links stay hidden until a script sets the data-open attribute, so a missing script leaves phone users without navigation.

sections.name: @media (prefers-reduced-motion:reduce)
sections.title: Motion limits, text fixes and small rules
sections.what: Shortens nearly all animations for users who ask for reduced motion. Also lifts faint grey text on dark panels, styles standings, roster tables, legal text, footer, the flip effect on the language switch, and the live or stale delay colours.
sections.why: Likely reason: reduced-motion support for accessibility, and the code comment says the grey text was raised to meet a contrast standard.
sections.watch_out: The reduced-motion rule forces nearly all animation to an almost instant length, so any animation that must run to convey meaning will lose that meaning for these users.

summary: Styles for the ALTER EGO interface pieces: cards, status badges, call tickets, timing tables, crew pages, navigation, onboarding and share cards.
purpose: Gives each shared interface piece its look, its focus outlines and its layout on phones and wider screens, using only the named colours and sizes from tokens.css.
why: Keeps the visual rules for shared pieces in one place so colours and spacing stay consistent. Reason for the exact split into these groups is not stated in the code.
how: The browser reads the file from top to bottom. Plain class rules set looks. Rules that match data attributes change colour when a component sets that attribute. Media rules change layout at set screen widths and when the user asks for less motion.
inputs: Class names and data attributes set by the React components in src/ui/components, and the named values defined in src/ui/tokens.css.
outputs: Visual styling only. Nothing is stored or returned. A wrong rule shows up as a wrong colour, size, spacing or layout on screen.
risks: Several rules use the :has selector, which some older browsers ignore, so option highlighting may not show there. Some crew-page rules apply to every button inside a crew page. Changing a shared name such as ui-badge changes every screen that uses it.
debug: If a piece looks unstyled, check that its class name matches exactly and that tokens.css is loaded. If a colour is wrong, compare the data attribute value with the matching rule here and with the dark theme in tokens.css. If the phone menu does not open, check these navigation rules and the script that sets data-open.
